fatal_errors: The proposed initially single-phase material conflicts with the target as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic alloy, which contains FCC and B2 phases.

The hypothesis assigns embrittlement to grain-boundary segregation and precipitation, whereas the target mechanism involves L12 ordering within FCC domains and jagged FCC/B2 phase boundaries without intergranular impurity segregation.
It omits the specific intermediate-temperature aging window and the critical comparison between approximately 600°C and 750°C.
It does not predict the defining non-monotonic ductile-brittle-ductile transition.
No supporting prior evidence is provided.
explanation: The response only identifies thermal treatment as a broad intervention and predicts generic toughness degradation. It largely repeats the conventional grain-boundary explanation that the requested comparison was meant to test against. It misses the dual-phase starting microstructure, enhanced L12 ordering, elevated antiphase-boundary energy and modulus, restricted cross-slip and planar slip, stress concentration at jagged phase-boundary tips, and ductility recovery through reduced ordering and ductile transition zones at higher aging temperature. The proposed experiment and falsification rule are too generic to distinguish grain-boundary embrittlement from the target phase-boundary/order-controlled mechanism; decisive measurements would localize dislocation pile-ups and crack initiation at jagged FCC/B2 boundary tips while excluding impurity segregation.
